unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12-LEVEL: B1.4 THEME 1: SCHOOL LIFE, CLASSROOM LIFE & EDUCATION

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will study on the concept of ''School Life, Classroom Life, and Education'', focusing on the sub-themes of challenges and coping with challenges for success, graduation and future plans after school, and national days and celebrations. They will create a multimedia project, such as a video diary or a digital book, documenting a fictional student's journey through school. This journey should include their struggles with academic and social challenges, strategies they use to manage stress, and their plans and aspirations for life after graduation. Students will also incorporate reflections on how their school community celebrates national days and traditions, highlighting the role these events play in fostering unity and pride. The project should creatively show the emotional highs and lows of school life, the importance of setting goals, and the value of celebrating milestones and cultural traditions, providing a relatable and inspiring narrative. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''school life, classroom life and education with its components such as challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 12 may know what challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 12, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''school life, classroom life and education'' in English from previous years such as ''boarding school, multicultural school, student-centred, supportive, varied and so on'' and also some structures such as ''The students are discussing a project in the seminar room right now. Students have an achievement test once a year. The optional school subjects are chosen by students.'' in English from the previous themes and/ or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''school life, classroom life and education with its components such as challenges and coping with challenges for success; graduation and future plans after school'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Their knowledge of the days of the week and holidays will help them learn and practise important national holidays such as ''the Republic Day of Türkiye''. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about coping strategies for challenges in English through a role-play activity by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Role-Playing Solutions The teacher tells the students that they role-play. S/He introduces the concept of addressing school-related challenges. The importance of understanding challenges such as exam stress, burnout, or lack of confidence is highlighted, along with effective strategies such as time management, goal setting, and self-discipline. Students work in pairs; one role represents a student experiencing challenges, while the other represents a teacher or counsellor offering guidance. The dialogue includes examples of challenges and strategies, incorporating key grammar points such as adverbial phrases (e.g., ''Tasks are completed efficiently in the morning'') and passive voice (e.g., ''Support is often provided by peers and mentors''). After preparation, pairs present their role-plays to the group. The teacher listens carefully and provides constructive feedback on target vocabulary usage, grammar accuracy, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students identify and categorise challenges and coping strategies in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Overcoming Challenges The teacher prepares a reading text for this activity. Students read the following text or another text like that and underline the challenges and coping strategies mentioned: ''Students sometimes face some challenges when studying. They learn how to set goals and manage their time. Some students take breaks to avoid stress. Teachers help them stay focused and complete tasks by giving advice and support. Self-discipline is also important to overcome problems''. After underlining, students categorise the words they identified: Challenges: Tiredness, stress Coping Strategies: set goals, manage time, take breaks, stay focused, self-discipline The teacher checks the categories and provides constructive and supportive feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
